messages:
Marta (Product): putting up a new idea for the Prompt Sets page: instead of per-row approve buttons, what if we surface a sticky approval rail when items are selected? Rail would show aggregated mini-metrics + 'Approve selected' + ability to pin a run for detailed review. Mock: https://figma.redwood/approval-rail

Kai (Design): interesting. the rail reduces visual noise and makes bulk actions more discoverable. my concern: users who just want to approve one item shouldn't have to select it first. we could show a lightweight inline affordance on hover for single-item quick approve and keep the rail for multi-select.

Sam (Eng): technically doable. rail is a simple sticky element using existing selection model. inline hover affordance needs careful hit-area handling for touch. performance wise both fine. pinning a run implies a small server-side pinnedRuns store (cheap).

Priya (Research): user research note: reviewers often toggle between metric glance and full diff. a pinned run helps keep context while scanning. also experimented with a "blind-review" toggle in labs — hides identifying metadata to reduce bias. might be useful for evals where we want unbiased raters.

Alex (Accessibility): a11y checklist: rail must be reachable via keyboard after any selection (focus trap?). prefer a skip-link so keyboard users can jump to the rail. rail actions need aria-pressed/aria-expanded states. pin action should announce via aria-live. For blind-review, ensure alt text is preserved and provide a clear way to unblind for keyboard users.

Kai (Design): copy ideas: rail header: "3 selected — summary"; approve CTA: "Approve selected (3)"; pin CTA: "Pin run"; blind-review toggle: "Blind review: on/off" with tooltip "hides user and prompt metadata". Also thinking of mini-sparkline vs numeric metrics for the rail.

Sam (Eng): sparks are cheap (SVG small) but rendering thousands could be heavy; in rail it's fine. inline rows could show numbers and small colored pill for regression count. heatmap suggestion: Priya proposed a subtle left-edge gradient to show per-run regression density. implementation: small CSS gradient + numeric badge.

Priya (Research): yes heatmap edge helps scanning. avoid red-only signaling. instead use semantic label: "Regression severity: low/medium/high" with tooltip examples. We measured 15% faster detection of bad runs with that pattern in hallway tests.

Jenny (DevEx): docs + onboarding: we should add a short tooltip tour the first time users select items describing rail, pinning, and blind-review. Also keyboard shortcuts: 'P' to pin focused run, 'A' to approve selected, and 'B' to toggle blind-review. Track analytics for these.

Alex (Accessibility): beware single-letter shortcuts conflicting with browser or screen reader muscle memory. Provide customizable shortcuts in user settings and ensure modifier keys recommended (e.g., Shift+P). Also announce shortcut availability in the help panel.

Marta (Product): decision proposal: implement sticky approval rail + inline quick-approve on hover + pinning + blind-review lab flag + heatmap edge + accessible shortcuts with modifier keys. Sam & Kai, can you prototype rail + inline affordance? Alex and Priya will validate a11y + bias tests. Jenny add docs + analytics events.

Sam (Eng): I'll spike the rail and pin backend this sprint. ETA: prototype and perf notes in 10 days.

Kai (Design): I'll iterate mocks and provide both desktop and touch behavior for inline affordance. Will include focus/skip-link states.

Priya (Research): I'll draft a small blind-review study to run with internal raters once prototype exists.

Alex (Accessibility): I'll draft the a11y acceptance checklist and run with the prototype.
